findings.finding: Graph `G -> F -> D` sends every incomplete chain to defense, while stages require first-failure routing. The preflight review, independent review and final disposition nodes have no explicit rejection/blocker edges. ARCHITECTURE-V1 lines 45–59, 91–104; PROMPTS-V1 lines 23–28.
findings.next_action: Orchestrator records the first incomplete stage, owner and recovery condition. Use withheld dispatch and authority outage as expected control failures, plus a missing-assets/setup failure. Successful routing sends setup to verifier/inventory and missing admission to integration; it does not ask defense to change working product code. Reject a malformed handoff before runtime and record the edge taken. Retain ambiguity as V1 evidence for V2.

findings.finding: Only verifier owns mutation and `run_episode`, but reviewer must independently reproduce in a new private environment. CASE assigns both owners without a transfer condition. ARCHITECTURE-V1 lines 39–40, 126; PROMPTS-V1 lines 72–73; CASE fields runtime_mutation_owner and independent_reproduction_owner.
findings.next_action: Orchestrator explicitly releases the verifier lease and assigns a separate reviewer episode/fixture before reproduction. Record old/new owner, fixture ID, times and allowed command. Demonstrate that reviewer starts after verifier cleanup; a second-owner request while the lease is held must wait or reject. Broad shell access is an experiment assumption, not implemented tool isolation.

findings.finding: V1 graph asks red team to inspect completed verifier evidence and then re-attack the defended state. Existing Run tears down API server, listeners and credentials before returning; it offers no live attach or bypass input. ARCHITECTURE-V1 lines 56–58, 102–103; run.go lines 184–212, 258–277, 577–600; command main.go flags.
findings.next_action: Keep normal hold probes classified as identical-credential retries, not two adaptive bypass variations. Ask verifier to show a supported way to execute the proposed variation against a defended fixture within existing scope. If none exists, record re-attack as unavailable, with exact missing adapter/contract input; do not call a new fresh episode a re-attack of the old state. V2 may predeclare probes for an in-episode hook or transfer a leased live environment, with independent review of any new harness.

findings.finding: Handoff has run/source/file hashes but no explicit case/contract revision, attempt ID, episode/control ID, dependency acceptance, gate result, enum contract or changed-evidence invalidation record. Hash validation does not prove an artifact belongs to the intended task or current contract. ARCHITECTURE-V1 lines 66–86; CASE contract_revision.
findings.next_action: For this trial preserve case hash in every input_refs and record episode IDs, control identity, acceptance condition and dependency dispositions in the orchestrator ledger. Submit an internally hash-valid handoff from a wrong contract or wrong control and require rejection. V2 should encode those bindings in the schema. No machine validator is supplied in V1; manual decisions/interventions must be counted.

findings.finding: Architecture separates threat/attribution/acceptance; existing report exposes one Verdict, passed stage list and Error. Many failing returns do not append the failed stage. No adapter defines how LOCAL_RUNTIME_DEFENDED, DECLINED and INCOMPLETE become the three dimensions. ARCHITECTURE-V1 lines 106–111; evidence.go lines 51–90; run.go lines 81, 105–124, 454–469, 599.
findings.next_action: Orchestrator/verifier classify from probes and completed chain, retaining the raw verdict and exact failing evidence. Positive can be BLOCKED/PROVEN with local acceptance only after all architecture requirements; skip-dispatch is LANDED/NOT_PROVEN; authority loss after dispatch is UNKNOWN/NOT_PROVEN/INCOMPLETE. A genuine already-denied baseline is NOT_LANDED/NOT_EXERCISED. Demonstrate expected nonzero controls complete their control tasks while the defense outcome still fails. Failure stage must be inferred and recorded where missing, with that intervention counted.

findings.finding: Retry/resume policy names operation IDs/readback but defines no prepared/running/ambiguous/terminal task states, ownership-transfer record, attempt counter consumption or lost-worker recovery. Current command creates a new environment and refuses nonempty output; its journal is durable within ephemeral API state, not a workflow resume service. ARCHITECTURE-V1 lines 130–140, 149–152; run.go lines 88–103, 184–212, 479–480, 551–554.
findings.next_action: Distinguish exact brain replay, fresh physical reproduction and recovery of the same operation. Interrupted run must remain INCOMPLETE and preserved. A fresh trial must have a new episode ID and baseline; it cannot resume the deleted environment. If same-state resume is not exercised, record it untested. V2 should define timeout/readback rules and counters before claiming resume support. Test a recorded interruption or lost worker without repeating an ambiguous actuator side effect.

findings.finding: CASE has required_action=null and forbids product changes, whereas the existing driver rejects every selected action except endpoint-lease-revoke and common defense prompt permits implementing an actuator. Fixed policy/recon/candidate expectations and most probe semantics are prose, rather than machine-bound options. CASE lines 13–20, 30; PROMPTS-V1 lines 51–58; run.go lines 338, 460–462.
findings.next_action: Treat this as one response-specific driver: natural selection is not forced, but its oracle cannot certify any alternative response. Preserve unexpected/declined selections; do not tune policy to pass. Record effective flags, resolved policy/recon, binary/source hashes and compare them to CASE. Any required new actuator/contract change becomes a new authorized version/trial, not an in-place V1 repair. Demonstrate wrong hold/latency/source options are caught by contract review.

findings.finding: Red team is to define successful baseline and legitimate controls, yet cannot certify the oracle; verifier independently inspects it and reviewer reviews it, without a stated dependency acceptance rule. The same existing harness produces observations and report. This is source/effect independence from defense, not diversity of all measurement code. ARCHITECTURE-V1 roles, review node; PROMPTS-V1 lines 41–47, 62–68, 72–77; evidence.go lines 97–129; runtime_fixture.py Downstream and Observer.
findings.next_action: Keep attack authoring, oracle review and final acceptance attributed separately. Reviewer checks raw bodies, nonce/counter deltas, hashes, B overlap, hold, source and replay rather than trusting summary. Fresh independent execution of the same reviewed code provides repetition, not a wholly separate oracle implementation. Existing tamper tests are useful but not this agent's executed evidence. Inspect proposed bypass or fallback without authoring it; reject any capability increase beyond A-only access.

findings.finding: During this preflight the orchestrator reported a red-team worker terminated with a provider safety flag before producing an artifact. V1 has no worker/provider-error branch or bounded role fallback. A lost worker is not a NOT_LANDED attack or a successful role handoff. Evidence is the direct orchestrator message received during review; no provider log or terminal artifact was supplied.
findings.next_action: Preserve the missing-output task and provider-failure classification separately from case outcomes, with no unchanged retry. An explicitly bounded orchestrator case-author fallback based on the existing owned-credential fixture may be independently reviewed; it is a roster/routing intervention, not red-team completion. Record author, source pins, capability limit, fallback budget and reviewer disposition. V2 needs an explicit provider-error edge and bounded fallback/stop criteria. The fallback itself has not yet been supplied or accepted by this reviewer.
